αἴαντός: Αἴας — Ajax, the Greek hero; masc. gen. sg.
βάλλοντες: βάλλω — throw, shoot, hit; pres. part. act. masc. nom. pl.: ’shooting’
βόε: βοῦς — ox, cow; masc. nom./acc. dual: ’the two oxen’
γίγνοντο: γίγνομαι — become, come to be; impf. 3 pl. mid., unaugmented (= ἐγίγνοντο): ’became, grew’
γναθμοῖο: γνάθμος (γνάθος) — jaw; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
δέδηε: δαίω — kindle, burn; perf. 3 sg. intrans., epic: ’is ablaze, burns’
δηϊόωντο: δηϊόω — cut down, slay; impf. 3 pl. pass., epic uncontracted, unaugmented (= Attic ἐδῃοῦντο): ’were being cut down’
δρακίος: Δράκιος — Dracius, an Epeian leader; masc. nom. sg.
εἰρυμέναι: ἐρύω — draw, drag, haul; perf. part. mid./pass. fem. nom. pl., epic εἰρυ- (Attic perfect has -σμ-: εἰρυσμέναι): ’drawn up’
εὐχήνωρ: Εὐχήνωρ — Euchenor, a Corinthian, son of Polyidus; masc. nom. sg.
θωὴν: θωή — a fine, penalty; fem. acc. sg.
κάλει: καλέω — call, summon; pres. imper. 2 sg. act., contracted from κάλεε: ’call!’
κάματός: κάματος — weariness, toil; masc. nom. sg., accent from the enclitic τε
κίθαριν: κίθαρις — lyre (later κιθάρα); fem. acc. sg.
κατακτὰς: κατακτείνω — kill, slay; aor. 2 part. act. masc. nom. sg., stem κτα- (= Attic κατακτανών): ’having killed’
κεράεσσι: κέρας — horn; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic κέρασι)
κορινθόθι: Κόρινθος — Corinth; place-name with locative suffix -θι: ’at Corinth’
λευγαλέως: λευγαλέος — pitiful, wretched; adv. λευγαλέως: ’pitiably, wretchedly’
λοκροὶ: Λοκροί — the Locrians; masc. nom. pl.
μάντιος: μάντις — seer, prophet; masc. gen. sg.
μίμνε: μίμνω — stay, remain, hold firm; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔμιμνε), epic reduplicated by-form of μένω: ’stayed’
μίμνει: μίμνω — stay, remain, wait; pres. 3 sg., epic reduplicated by-form of μένω
μείλινα: μείλινος — of ash-wood; neut. acc. pl.
μενεπτόλεμός: μενεπτόλεμος — steadfast in battle, standing firm against the foe; masc. nom. sg., accent from the enclitic τε
μητρυιῆς: μητρυιά — stepmother; fem. gen. sg., Ionic -ῆς (= Attic -ᾶς)
μιμνήσκοντο: μιμνήσκομαι — remember, be mindful of (+ gen.); impf. 3 pl. mid., unaugmented (= ἐμιμνήσκοντο): ’were thinking of’
νειῷ: νειός — fallow field; fem. dat. sg.
νούσῳ: νοῦσος (Attic νόσος) — sickness, disease; fem. dat. sg.
νοῦσόν: νοῦσος (Attic νόσος) — sickness, disease; fem. acc. sg.
οἴνοπε: οἴνοψ — wine-faced, having the look of wine (the colour meant is unsettled); adj., masc. nom./acc. dual
πέσωμεν: πίπτω — fall, fall upon; aor. subj. 1 pl. (aor. ἔπεσον), with κεν in an alternative question: ’we should fall’
παραρρητοῖσι: παράρρητος — persuasive, winning one over by words (elsewhere also ’talked round’); neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις), as a noun: ’words of persuasion’ (sense uncertain)
παρβεβαῶτε: παραβαίνω — stand beside, go beside; perf. part. act. masc. nom. dual, epic παρβ- for παραβ-: ’standing side by side’
παφλαγόνεσσι: Παφλαγόνες — the Paphlagonians; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic -σι)
περιίδμεναι: περίοιδα — know better than, surpass in knowledge (+ gen.); inf., epic -ίδμεναι (= Attic περιειδέναι)
πολυΐδου: Πολύϊδος — Polyidus, a Corinthian seer; masc. gen. sg.
πολύϊδος: Πολύϊδος — Polyidus, a Corinthian seer; masc. nom. sg.
προλελεγμένοι: προλέγω — pick out, choose beforehand; perf. part. mid./pass. masc. nom. pl.: ’picked out, chosen’
πρυμνοῖσιν: πρυμνός — hindmost, at the base; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις): ’at the base’
πυκινὰς: πυκινός — thick, close-packed, dense; fem. acc. pl.
σθένει: σθένος — strength, might; neut. dat. sg.: ’in strength, with might’
στέφανος: στέφανος — wreath, ring, encircling band; masc. nom. sg., of a ring of war
στυγερήν: στυγερός — hateful, loathsome; fem. acc. sg., Ionic -ην (= Attic -άν)
συνεκλόνεον: συγκλονέω — throw into confusion, drive in panic; impf. 3 pl., uncontracted (= Attic συνεκλόνουν), augment inside the compound: ’were driving into panic’
τέλσον: τέλσον — boundary, end of the furrow, headland; neut. acc. sg.
τέμει: τέμνω — cut; pres. 3 sg., epic by-form (= Attic τέμνει): ’cuts’
τελαμωνίου: Τελαμώνιος — son of Telamon, Telamonian (of Ajax); masc. gen. sg. (Attic form the same)
τελαμωνιάδῃ: Τελαμωνιάδης — son of Telamon, i.e. Ajax (patronymic); masc. dat. sg.
τιθεῖ: τίθημι — put, place; pres. 3 sg., epic contracted (= Attic τίθησι)
τιταίνετον: τιταίνω — stretch, draw, pull; pres. 3 dual act.: ’the two pull’
φαιδιμόεντες: φαιδιμόεις — shining, glorious; masc. nom. pl., stem φαιδιμοεντ-
φείδας: Φείδας — Pheidas, an Athenian leader; masc. nom. sg.
φθίων: Φθῖοι — the Phthians, men of Phthia; masc. gen. pl.
φθῖοι: Φθῖοι — the Phthians, men of Phthia; masc. nom. pl.
χαλκήρεας: χαλκήρης — fitted with bronze; masc./fem. acc. pl. (two-ending adj.)
χθαμαλώτατον: χθαμαλός — low, low-lying; superl. χθαμαλώτατον, neut. nom. sg., predicate: ’lowest’
χθιζὸν: χθιζός — of yesterday, yesterday’s; neut. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun
ἀλέεινεν: ἀλεείνω — avoid, shun, evade; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (Attic would lengthen to η-): ’evaded’
ἀμφίων: Ἀμφίων — Amphion, an Epeian leader; masc. nom. sg.
ἀνέγνω: ἀναγιγνώσκω — know for certain, recognise; aor. 3 sg., augment inside the compound (ἀν-έ-γνω): ’recognised’, or gnomic ’recognises’
ἀνακηκίει: ἀνακηκίω — gush up, well up; pres. 3 sg., stem κηκι-: ’wells up’
ἀπήμονες: ἀπήμων — unharmed, unscathed, safe; adj., masc. nom. pl.
ἀποστήσωνται: ἀφίστημι — set apart; mid. of a debt, exact or get paid back (sense uncertain); aor. subj. 3 pl. mid., epic ἀπο- (= ἀφ-), in a fear clause: ’lest they exact’
ἀργαλέῃ: ἀργαλέος — hard, grievous, painful; fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ
ἀφεστᾶσιν: ἀφίστημι — stand away, stand aloof; perf. 3 pl. act. intrans., contracted (= Attic ἀφεστήκασι): ’stand aloof’
ἀφνειός: ἀφνειός — rich, wealthy; masc. nom. sg.
ἄρά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, accented ἄρά before an enclitic
ἐΰς: ἐΰς (ἠΰς) — good, brave, noble; masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ἀγαθός)
ἐδέδμητο: δέμω — build; plpf. 3 sg. pass. (perf. δέδμημαι; Attic uses οἰκοδομέω, ᾠκοδόμητο): ’had been built’
ἐλάνθανον: λανθάνω — escape notice, be unseen; impf. 3 pl., + supplementary part.: ’did it unnoticed’
ἐξεδέχοντο: ἐκδέχομαι — take from, receive; impf. 3 pl. mid.: ’took over, received’
ἐπέπυστο: πυνθάνομαι — learn, hear, find out; plpf. 3 sg. (perf. πέπυσμαι) with past sense: ’had learned, knew’
ἐπαυρίσκοντ: ἐπαυρίσκω — enjoy, gain benefit from (+ gen.); pres. 3 pl. mid., elided (ἐπαυρίσκοντ’ = ἐπαυρίσκονται; ἐπαυρίσκοντο is also possible): ’have the benefit’
ἐπιφρασσαίμεθα: ἐπιφράζομαι — consider, devise, think out; aor. opt. 1 pl. mid., epic σσ, with ἂν potential: ’we might consider’
ἐριώπιδος: Ἐριῶπις — Eriopis, wife of Oileus; fem. gen. sg.
ἐχώρησαν: χωρέω — give way, retire, retreat; aor. 3 pl., with κε past potential: ’would have retreated’
ἑλκεχίτωνες: ἑλκεχίτων — with trailing tunic, long-robed; masc. nom. pl. (epithet of the Ionians)
ἑτέρῳ: ἕτερος — the other (of two), another; masc. dat. sg.
ἔλθωμεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. subj. 1 pl. (aor. ἦλθον), with κεν in an alternative question: ’we should come’
ἕταροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl., epic by-form ἕταροι (= ἑταῖροι)
ἰάονες: Ἴαονες — the Ionians; masc. nom. pl., epic Ἰάονες (= Attic Ἴωνες)
ἰφίκλοιο: Ἴφικλος — Iphiclus, father of Podarces; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἱεμένω: ἵεμαι — be eager, strain forward, press on; pres. part. mid. masc. dual: ’straining on’
ἱπποδασείας: ἱπποδασύς — thick with horsehair, horse-crested; adj., fem. acc. pl., epic -είας (= Attic -εῖας)
ὀλοὴν: ὀλοός — deadly, destructive; fem. acc. sg.
ὀϊλεύς: Ὀϊλεύς — Oileus, father of the lesser Ajax; masc. nom. sg.
ὀϊλιάδῃ: Ὀϊλιάδης — son of Oileus, i.e. the lesser Ajax (patronymic); masc. dat. sg.
ὄτρυν: ὀτρύνω — urge on, rouse; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (ὄτρυν’ = ὤτρυνε): ’urged on’
ὦλκα: ὦλξ (ὄλκος) — furrow; masc. acc. sg., epic (cf. Attic αὖλαξ)
ὦσαι: ὠθέω — push, thrust, drive back; aor. inf. act.: ’to drive back’
ῥήγνυντο: ῥήγνυμι — break; mid. break through; impf. 3 pl. mid.: ’broke through’
ῥηξάμενος: ῥήγνυμι — break; mid. break through; aor. part. mid. masc. nom. sg.: ’having broken through’

__broaden__.βίας: βία — force, might, violence; fem. acc. pl., the plural for a people’s might: ’the might (of the Trojans)’ · also Βίας — Bias, an Athenian leader; masc. nom. sg.
__broaden__.γνωτὸν: γνωτός — known, plain, knowable (verbal adj. of γιγνώσκω); neut. nom. sg., predicate: ’known, plain’ · also masc. acc. sg. as a noun: ’kinsman, brother’
__broaden__.ζυγὸν: ζυγόν — yoke; neut. acc. sg., after ὑπό in tmesis with ἤγαγεν: ’under the yoke’ · also neut. acc. sg., after ὑπέρ: ’over the yoke’ (ὑπὲρ ζυγόν) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of ἦεν (the yoke of a lyre): ’a yoke’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of ἐέργει: ’the yoke’ (ζυγὸν … ἐέργει ’the yoke keeps (them) apart’)
__broaden__.μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after; + acc.: ’to, among’ (motion) · also + dat.: ’among’ (μετ’ ἀθανάτοισιν) · also + acc., ’next after’ (μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα) · also + acc., ’after, in pursuit of’ · also + gen.: ’among’ (μετ’ Ἀχαιῶν ’among the Achaeans’)
__broaden__.οἷσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις), agreeing with ἅρμασιν: ’its own’ · also masc. dat. pl., used as a noun: ’his own (men)’ · also relative ὅς, masc. dat. pl.: ’on whom’ (οἷσιν ἐπὶ … θῆκε ’on whom … set’) · also relative, dat. pl. of interest: ’for whom’ (οἷσιν ἀνάγκη ’for whom there is need’) · also relative, neut. dat. pl. of means: ’with which’ (οἷσιν … ῥήγνυντο ’with which they broke’)
__broaden__.οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg. · also οἶος printed for οἰός (οἶς) — sheep; gen. sg. οἰός: ’of a sheep’ (οἰὸς ἄωτος ’sheep’s wool’)
__broaden__.ὅττί: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; neut. acc. sg. ὅττι (doubled τ), accented before the enclitic κεν · also ὅττι = ὅτι, ’that’, after a verb of knowing (οὐδέ τι ᾔδη ὅττι … ’nor did he know that …’)
